newsitem.title: USA: Bosnia arms depend on firing of officials - U.S.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia arms depend on firing of officials - U.S.

text.p: The United States on Friday pressed Bosnian Federation President Kresimir Zubak to take the final step to dismiss two senior defence officials so a massive shipment of U.S. arms can be delivered.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Zubak, who heads the Moslem-Croat federation that is one of two entities in Bosnia, has been reluctant to fire the officials, including one with strong ties to Iran.

Up to now, Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic was seen as the obstacle. But Izetbegovic finally presented the documents on Friday that would remove Deputy Minister Hasan Cengic and Minister Vladimir Soljic from office and "this issue is now clearly in the hands of President Zubak," Burns said.

"Once Mr. Zubak acts on this recommendation, and once these two individuals are no longer at the Federation Defence Ministry, then the ship the American Condor, which is currently off Ploce Harbour, will dock at Ploce Harbour and will off-load its military assistance for the federation."

A cargo vessel with $100 million dollars worth of military equipment bound for Bosnia has been idling in the Adriatic, waiting for Sarajevo to remove Cengic, since Oct. 24. At talks in Paris this week, Secretary of State Warren Christopher and other U.S. officials urged Zubak to take action.

But Burns said Zubak "has indicated a general reluctance to make a decision for a variety of reasons because there are other factors that they've got to look at here." He noted the problems the three members of Bosnia's rotating presidency -- Zubak, a Croat; Izetbegovic, a Moslem; and Momcilo Krajisnik, a Serb -- have had in working out a council of ministers.
The firing of the defence officials "may or may not be caught up in those deliberations," Burns said.

"But it's such an important issue for the United States that we wanted to make clear today that now that President Izetbegovic, after several weeks of deliberations, has come forward and has said that he wants the two removed, his prime minister wants the two removed, his vice president wants the two removed, it now only rests for Mr. Zubak to agree with this decision."
Burns said the action can be taken by Zubak by executive authority and does not require parliamentary approval.

"We maintain our own position ... that if the United States is going to be delivering $100 million worth of military hardware to the federation we have a right to insist that one of the senior ... members of the federation defence establishment -- not be someone who has very close ties to the government of Iran," he said.

The United States is sponsoring a $400 million "train and equip" programme in Bosnia intended to bring the country's fledgling Moslem-Croat Federation army up to military parity with separate Bosnian Serb armed forces. But it made the programme contingent on departure of foreign Islamic fighters, known as mujahedin, from Bosnia. Most are reported to have left the country.
